title: Contextual chunk embeddings + low-signal gating; lift 8-chunk cap
description:
Embed passage chunks WITH document context prepended (title, source, date, section heading) instead of naked text, gate low-signal chunks out of the index, and lift the 8-chunk cap that currently makes only the first ~1,440 words of long reports searchable. Based on Anthropic's contextual-retrieval result, which Cerebras applied as "bursting."

BLOCKED BY: hybrid-lexical epic (needs its document-frequency table for IDF gating) and distillation epic (both change embedding input — batch into ONE corpus re-embed).

## Current state (verified 2026-07-19)

- `_prepare_chunks` (`src/papyrus_knowledge_query/vector_index.py:720-756`) embeds the raw cleaned chunk text only. Title/subtitle/summary are threaded in as `reference_metadata_payload` but go only into metadata, never the embedded string.
- `_chunk_text` (`engine.py:2954-2982`) already captures each chunk's section `heading` — currently DISCARDED at index time (`_prepare_chunks` doesn't read it).
- Gating today: 120-char floor (`vector_index.py:731`) and a hard cap `max_chunks_per_reference: 8` (`VectorIndexOptions`, `vector_index.py:79`); at `chunk_words: 180` that's ~1,440 words of coverage per reference.
- Chunk keys are POSITIONAL: `sha256(lineageId:storagePath:chunkIndex)` (`vector_index.py:733`) — changing embedded text does NOT change keys, so sync dedup logic keyed on vector keys will consider unchanged-position chunks "already present". A forced rebuild is required for the new embeddings to take effect (this is expected; see rebuild coupling).

## Design decisions (current thinking — challenge them if you have better information)

1. **Contextual prefix**: embed `f"{title} — {subtitle or source_org} ({published_date}). Section: {heading}.

{chunk_text}"`. Omit empty parts cleanly. Cap the prefix portion at 300 chars. `source_org`/`published_date` come from reference fields/distillation artifact when present; degrade gracefully.
2. **Stored metadata `text`/`summary` stay the RAW chunk** — rendered evidence must not show the synthetic prefix.
3. **Gating (replaces the bare 120-char floor)**: reject a chunk if (a) < 40 tokens, OR (b) stopword ratio > 0.65, OR (c) IDF-sum below threshold, where IDF comes from the document-frequency table produced by the lexical-index build (import from `lexical_index.py`; if the DF table is unavailable, skip criterion (c) and log). All thresholds configurable via `VectorIndexOptions`.
4. **Cap**: raise `max_chunks_per_reference` default 8 → 64 (still configurable). With gating, indexing full documents is safe.
5. **Audit-first rollout**: add a dry-run mode that reports per-reference gated-chunk counts and total vector count delta WITHOUT writing, so we can sanity-check thresholds against the real corpus before the rebuild.

## Files to modify

- `src/papyrus_knowledge_query/vector_index.py` — `_prepare_chunks` (prefix + heading threading + gating), `VectorIndexOptions` (cap + thresholds), audit reporting.
- `src/papyrus_knowledge_query/lexical_index.py` — expose the DF/IDF table for reuse.
- Tests: prefix-format tests (empty-part handling), gating boundary tests, a fixture long-document test proving chunks beyond position 8 are now indexed, raw-text-in-metadata regression test.

## What could go wrong

- **Over-gating loses recall silently.** This is why audit-first is mandatory: run the dry-run against the real corpus, eyeball what gets dropped, then tune. Log gated counts at sync time permanently.
- **Prefix pollution of evidence**: if any code path reads embedded text instead of metadata text for display, the synthetic prefix leaks into rendered evidence. Grep consumers of chunk `text` metadata before assuming.
- **Vector count growth**: lifting the cap multiplies vectors for long documents (cost is per-vector storage + query; S3 Vectors is cheap, but log the delta in the audit).
- **Rebuild discipline**: positional keys mean a plain `sync` will NOT refresh existing chunks' embeddings. The rollout requires `--action rebuild` (or force), batched with the distillation epic's re-embed. One rebuild, not two.
- **Token counting for the 40-token floor**: tiktoken is OPTIONAL in the Lambda environment; the tokens module has a regex fallback (`src/papyrus_knowledge_query/tokens.py`) — use it, don't import tiktoken directly.

## Acceptance criteria

- A distinctive passage at word ~3,000 of a long fixture document is findable via semantic search after rebuild.
- "sounds good, thanks!"-grade chunks (short, common-token) are gated out; a short chunk containing a rare identifier survives (IDF criterion working).
- Rendered evidence shows no synthetic prefixes.

## Out of scope

Re-chunking strategy changes (chunk size stays 180 words), insight-message vectors (reference passages only for v1), the rebuild execution itself (coordinate with distillation epic).
